sources.cite: GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18 documentation, OpenID Connect
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: workflows exchange an OIDC token for a short-lived cloud token valid for a single job instead of storing long-lived cloud credentials as secrets; the cloud role's trust conditions match the token's subject, such as repository, environment and branch.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: provenance describes who built an artifact, how and from what inputs; Build L1 has provenance, L2 a hosted build platform that signs it, L3 hardened builds.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: an admission controller that validates image signatures and attestations against ClusterImagePolicy resources in opted-in namespaces, with a warn mode.

sources.cite: Anchore open source documentation, Syft: Attestation
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: syft attest generates an SBOM as a signed in-toto attestation stored in the registry alongside the image.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You own the shared CI/CD pipeline at Calder Retail, a fictional retailer whose platform builds images for 40 services. A security review lands this week.
handover: Every pipeline uses one long-lived cloud admin key stored as a CI secret.
Images are pushed unsigned; nothing records how they were built.
howItWorks: The console shows the alert queue, the event log and each asset's status.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: a dependency in one repository's build steals the key; the attacker creates crypto-mining instances across the account.
Check-in 3: a replaced checkout image with a card skimmer runs for six hours before anyone notices.
Check-in 4: a week after the advisory, two affected images are still unpatched; nobody knew they used the library.

identPrompt.title: One admin key for 40 pipelines
identPrompt.context: A leaked key would give an attacker the whole cloud account.

choices.label: Replace the key with OIDC federation: each job exchanges its token for a short-lived credential on a role scoped to its repository and environment, with only the permissions it needs; then revoke the old key
choices.feedback: Short-lived tokens from OIDC remove long-lived secrets; trust scoped by repository and environment keeps each pipeline to its own role.

choices.label: Keep the key but rotate it every quarter
choices.feedback: Rotation shortens exposure, but it is still one admin key for everyone.

choices.label: Keep the key; CI secrets are encrypted
choices.feedback: Any compromised pipeline holds full cloud access.

signPrompt.title: Images nobody can verify
signPrompt.context: Anyone with push rights could replace an image.

choices.label: Build on the hosted builder that signs provenance, sign images with cosign, and have the policy controller admit only images signed by the pipeline, in warn mode first

effects.log: Signed images with provenance; admission verifies them.

choices.feedback: Signed provenance records who built what from which inputs; verification at admission is what makes signing a control.

choices.label: Sign images but do not verify them anywhere
choices.feedback: A signature nobody checks stops nothing.

choices.label: Skip signing; the registry requires a login
choices.feedback: A stolen push credential lets an attacker replace any image.

sbomPrompt.title: Which images contain the flawed library?
sbomPrompt.context: A critical advisory names a logging library; nobody knows which images include it.

choices.label: Generate an SBOM for every image with syft attest, stored as a signed attestation with the image, and query them for the advisory

effects.log: Affected images are listed in minutes.

choices.feedback: An SBOM attached to each image answers 'where is this library?' when an advisory lands.

choices.label: Save SBOMs as build artifacts in the CI system
choices.feedback: They exist, but are detached from the images and expire with build logs.

choices.label: Skip SBOMs; scan images when advisories arrive
choices.feedback: Every advisory means rescanning 40 services by hand.

parts.label: Identity
parts.criteria: OIDC federation to scoped, short-lived roles; the admin key revoked.
parts.modelAnswer: Each pipeline now gets a short-lived credential for its own role; the shared admin key is revoked.

parts.label: Artifacts
parts.criteria: Signed images and provenance verified at admission; SBOM attestations.
parts.modelAnswer: Images and provenance are signed and verified by the policy controller; each image carries a signed SBOM.

scoring.modelReasoning: A secure pipeline holds no long-lived shared secrets: OIDC gives each job a short-lived credential scoped to its role. Signed provenance records how artifacts were built, and verification at admission makes signatures a control. SBOM attestations stored with images answer advisories quickly.
